title: Left 4 Dead 2 writer says Valve intentionally 'leaked' its cinematic trailer to get around ESRB rules: 'I think we can't get trouble for that now'
summary: It's strange to think about in hindsight, but Left 4 Dead 2 was a controversial game in the run-up to its release in November 2009—just one year after the original Left 4 Dead laid the foundations for today's enormous cooperative gaming scene. Indeed, it was that rapid turnaround, combined with the fact that the first Left 4 Dead was a relatively short game, which led to accusations that Left 4 Dead 2 was nothing more than a cynical ploy by Valve to cash in on the success of the first.
author: Rick Lane
keyHighlights: It's strange to think about in hindsight, but Left 4 Dead 2 was a controversial game in the run-up to its release in November 2009—just one year after the original Left 4 Dead laid the foundations for today's enormous cooperative gaming scene.
One reason was that, at the time, Valve had run-ins with numerous countries and ratings boards over the series' depictions of violence and use of profane language.
Language or violence that might land a game a 'Mature' rating could result in a trailer that depicted the same things being banned outright.
fullContent: It's strange to think about in hindsight, but Left 4 Dead 2 was a controversial game in the run-up to its release in November 2009—just one year after the original Left 4 Dead laid the foundations for today's enormous cooperative gaming scene. Indeed, it was that rapid turnaround, combined with the fact that the first Left 4 Dead was a relatively short game, which led to accusations that Left 4 Dead 2 was nothing more than a cynical ploy by Valve to cash in on the success of the first.

Ultimately, Left 4 Dead 2 would prove a worthy follow-up to Valve's cooperative blaster. But it turns out there was some skulduggery afoot behind the scenes on Left 4 Dead 2, just not the kind that fans suspected. Shortly before the sequel's launch, a cinematic trailer—which would ultimately serve as Left 4 Dead 2's introductory cutscene—leaked onto the Internet. Now, it's been revealed that this 'leak' was orchestrated by Valve to evade the censorious watch of the Entertainment Software Ratings Board.

This is according to former Valve writer and Left 4 Dead designer Chet Faliszek, who revealed Valve's deliberate leak in a YouTube video about cut Left 4 Dead voice lines (via Ars Technica ). In the video, Faliszek explains why Left 4 Dead 2 had a large number of voice lines cut from the final game. One reason was that, at the time, Valve had run-ins with numerous countries and ratings boards over the series' depictions of violence and use of profane language.

"You have to remember, especially during Left 4 Dead 1 and Left 4 Dead 2 time, Valve was in fights with the ESRB, with Australia, with Germany, with a bunch of countries about the profanity in the game, or the violence," he explains. "One of [Valve's] lawyers stepped in and said that us writers needed to be babysat on this. And so [the] first thing we did was, well, we made sure there was no profanity in there that crosses the line—basically F-bombs."

Faliszek personally believed that, when it comes to censorship of language and depictions of violence, "you push it and have the ESRB push back". But Valve's lawyer felt differently and Faliszek went along with it. However, the ESRB's regulatory oversight didn't just cover games, but extended to the marketing material for those games. And unlike today, the ESRB had different regulatory rules for trailers and games. Language or violence that might land a game a 'Mature' rating could result in a trailer that depicted the same things being banned outright.

title: Before HBO's The Last Of Us, An Entirely Different Adaptation Was Proposed
summary: Naughty Dog's first effort to adapt The Last of Us for the screen was not as an HBO TV show, but a movie, a fact that recently began doing the rounds again on social media. Like with many Hollywood productions, The Last of Us had a tumultuous, long development period as a movie before it was ultimately abandoned in favor of what is now a hit series.
author: Eddie Makuch
keyHighlights: Naughty Dog's first effort to adapt The Last of Us for the screen was not as an HBO TV show, but a movie, a fact that recently began doing the rounds again on social media.

People across X recently discovered a post from Sony Pictures in 2014 declaring that The Last of Us was "soon to be a major motion picture."  This was a real, studio-sponsored image, not a fan mock-up.
That The Last of Us was originally going to be a movie is not surprising given how many video game movies came before it and how many have been released since (with varying degrees of success).
fullContent: Naughty Dog's first effort to adapt The Last of Us for the screen was not as an HBO TV show, but a movie, a fact that recently began doing the rounds again on social media. Like with many Hollywood productions, The Last of Us had a tumultuous, long development period as a movie before it was ultimately abandoned in favor of what is now a hit series.

While not everyone agrees with the creative departures from the source material for the TV series on HBO, it's undeniably a success and one of HBO's biggest hits lately. Let's look back at how The Last of Us originated as a movie and run through the key developments that led to it becoming a TV show.
People across X recently discovered a post from Sony Pictures in 2014 declaring that The Last of Us was "soon to be a major motion picture."

This was a real, studio-sponsored image, not a fan mock-up. There was officially produced key art, showing Ellie wielding a knife. There was a "secret panel" at San Diego Comic-Con that year featuring director Sam Raimi, who was originally attached to produce the movie, having already had huge success at Sony with his Spider-Man films.
That The Last of Us was originally going to be a movie is not surprising given how many video game movies came before it and how many have been released since (with varying degrees of success).

summary: After a quiet few months, September finally hits the gas, and our list of monthly PC game happenings is filled with brand new adventures, series continuations, 1.0 updates, and events galore. I'm still playing catch-up after Gamescom, and now we've got Tokyo Game Show queued up soon.

fullContent: After a quiet few months, September finally hits the gas, and our list of monthly PC game happenings is filled with brand new adventures, series continuations, 1.0 updates, and events galore. I'm still playing catch-up after Gamescom, and now we've got Tokyo Game Show queued up soon. It's the same schedule every year, but somehow I'm always caught off guard.

The Blood of Dawnwalker kicked off the month with a delightfully dismal vampire RPG from the Witcher veterans at Rebel Wolves. Then you've got all month to suck blood as Coen (or be a good two-shoes and abstain, I guess) before Silent Hill: Townfall and Control Resonant launch on the same damn day. It seems everything I've been waiting all year to play has crammed into this 4-week window, and that's not even counting all the big updates.

The Witcher 3 Remastered is easily among the most notable updates, and everyone who owns the original gets the RPG's makeover for free (along with its DLC). It'll be my first time playing, so between that and Valheim 1.0, I'll be plenty busy until 2027.

Steam | I've been loving The Blood of Dawnwalker, but you don't have to take my broody, vampire-obsessed word for it. Shaun called it "one of best action RPGs [he's] played in years," in his Blood of Dawnwalker review .

Steam | I have to say it every time: I still can't believe we're in a Silent Hill renaissance. I'm hoping Townfall continues this trend of one banger release after another, and from how Fraser explains his time as Simon in a hellish version of Scotland, it has a chance.

title: How To Complete The Cycle Of Love In The Blood Of Dawnwalker - Xanthe Boss Guide
summary: Are you befuddled by the tasks in The Cycle of Love in The Blood of Dawnwalker ? This quest, which is the conclusion of your battles against Xanthe, takes place in a keep.
author: Jason Rodriguez
keyHighlights: Are you befuddled by the tasks in The Cycle of Love in The Blood of Dawnwalker ?
Down the line, one of Brencis’ soldiers, Leonard, will show up and ask you to eliminate Xanthe.
With a bit of luck and skill, you might just be able to finish her off there.
fullContent: Are you befuddled by the tasks in The Cycle of Love in The Blood of Dawnwalker ? This quest, which is the conclusion of your battles against Xanthe, takes place in a keep. Along the way, you have to illuminate your surroundings to access new pathways. Oh, and you also have to consider Xanthe’s offer at the end. Our guide has all the info that you need, but be ready for some minor spoilers , too.

The Blood of Dawnwalker Cycle of Love quest appears in your journal once you’ve maxed out Xanthe’s anger toward you. As such, you have to spend some time in the campaign taking out her blood guards and disrupting her research into ancient ruins.

Down the line, one of Brencis’ soldiers, Leonard, will show up and ask you to eliminate Xanthe. He’ll give you a lantern that grants access to her lair, a foreboding castle called Howling Keep. Be ready because you’re about to venture into one of the creepiest areas in the game.
Note 1: Howling Keep is west of Tantari Woods. Once the quest is active, track the “Get to the mansion” objective to make the marker appear on your map.
Note 2: Xanthe also appears in the Svartrau City cathedral at night, and only once fairly early in the game. With a bit of luck and skill, you might just be able to finish her off there.

title: 14 Predictions for the September 2026 Nintendo Direct and Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct
summary: Nintendo is hosting two Directs in the coming days , and it’s pretty much all I’ve been thinking about since the announcement. On Tuesday, September 8, it’s The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, followed by a more general Nintendo Direct on Wednesday, September 9.
author: Logan Plant
keyHighlights: Nintendo is hosting two Directs in the coming days , and it’s pretty much all I’ve been thinking about since the announcement.
This will undoubtedly be the centerpiece of the presentation.

You don’t set the internet’s imagination on fire with a 10-second tease of Link’s treehouse if you don’t have really satisfying answers to share when you do finally pull the curtain back, and I expect the Ocarina of Time remake to be a pretty big deal.
fullContent: Nintendo is hosting two Directs in the coming days , and it’s pretty much all I’ve been thinking about since the announcement. On Tuesday, September 8, it’s The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, followed by a more general Nintendo Direct on Wednesday, September 9. While we wait, it's predictions time!

Before we start, a couple of disclaimers: these are all purely my guesses based on public information and my analysis of Nintendo’s release patterns, and nothing more. Nothing here is based on any inside information. But, I will be discussing a couple of relevant leaks over the last few months, so if you have been steering clear of information like that, you may not want to read on.

Zelda is my favorite series, so I’m buzzing thinking about all the possibilities we could see Tuesday morning. But I’m trying to keep things realistic in this piece and only sharing predictions that I think have a legitimate chance of happening.

This will undoubtedly be the centerpiece of the presentation. We’ve only seen a few seconds of footage of the Ocarina of Time remake , which is set to come out in 2026. So, now’s the time for the full reveal trailer and release date. I can’t wait for this one; my imagination has been running wild over this remake for the last three months, and we’re finally going to see more about the scope of this remake. Is it faithful, or more of a reimagining? What does the kingdom of Hyrule look like beyond Link’s treehouse? All that and more will likely be answered by a more conventional trailer that gives us a proper look at the remake.

I don’t know exactly what Ocarina of Time will look like, but the teaser trailer from earlier this year tells me Nintendo is very confident in this game. You don’t set the internet’s imagination on fire with a 10-second tease of Link’s treehouse if you don’t have really satisfying answers to share when you do finally pull the curtain back, and I expect the Ocarina of Time remake to be a pretty big deal.

title: 'No One Puts Double Fine Out of Business Except for Me' — Tim Schafer Explains How He Kept Double Fine Afloat After Leaving Xbox
summary: Tim Schafer, game designer and founder of Psychonauts developer Double Fine, gave a strong response after Xbox divested the studio as part of its massive restructuring efforts this summer.
author: Virginia Glaze
keyHighlights: Tim Schafer, game designer and founder of Psychonauts developer Double Fine, gave a strong response after Xbox divested the studio as part of its massive restructuring efforts this summer.
"No one puts Double Fine out of business except for me," he continued.

That isn’t stopping it from making more games, though, as the developer recently published a Kickstarter for its next project — with the addendum that if it raises $100 million, they’ll also make Brutal Legend 2.
fullContent: Tim Schafer, game designer and founder of Psychonauts developer Double Fine, gave a strong response after Xbox divested the studio as part of its massive restructuring efforts this summer.

Speaking with Bloomberg's Jason Schreier in a September 2026 interview , Schafer admitted that he knew something was up before Xbox’s divestment was officially announced — but he wasn’t about to go down without a fight.

"You’re like, 'Wait a second, we’re not going out like this,'" Schafer explained. "Some people said, 'I’m checking out, this is one too many battles for me.’ But for the rest of us, it’s like a creative awakening."

"No one puts Double Fine out of business except for me," he continued. "Asha’s not going to shoot my dog. I’m going to shoot it. But I’m not going to shoot it, because it’s going to do great. A lot of people want to walk the dog."

Thankfully, Double Fine was able to retain its intellectual property and become fully independent, though it did have to lay off a quarter of its staff as a result of this change. That isn’t stopping it from making more games, though, as the developer recently published a Kickstarter for its next project — with the addendum that if it raises $100 million, they’ll also make Brutal Legend 2.

fullContent: DC fans are convinced the DCU's Wonder Woman will be played by Adria Arjona after she posted a video of her workout routine ahead of Man of Tomorrow .

As the DCU navigates its ups and downs , all eyes are on DC Studios co-CEO and director James Gunn to deliver next year's Superman sequel. Arjona is just one part of the equation that will help bring David Corenswet's Last Son of Krypton back to the big screen, but fans think she knows more than she's letting on when it comes to the part she'll play in the wider DCU.

Mixed in with a variety of other superhero parts – including Milly Alcock's Supergirl , Aaron Pierre's John Stewart , and Xolo Maridueña as Blue Beetle – Arjona was previously said to be playing the role of DC deep cut Maxima . She reportedly landed the part in April of this year, but fans think Gunn and company are misleading fans in hopes of a big Sadie Sink/Spider-Man-style surprise with Man of Tomorrow.

Rumors that her role would eventually be revealed as Wonder Woman surfaced shortly after her casting, but nothing has stoked the flames quite like a video posted by Women's Health yesterday . The seven-minute highlight showed Arjona's "intense boxing and strength workout," letting viewers peek into how she trains for the parts she plays. Although she explicitly mentioned that training helped her prepare to play Celeste in Onslaught, a later segment brings her rumored DC career into focus.

"I've never felt strong, but it's hard," Arjona said as headlines related to Wonder Woman rumors flased on the screen. "Well, I think the excitement of playing the woman I'm playing gives me everything I need to wake up. Physically, it's exhausting, but it's all for the better good. The better good? Is that English? The greater good!"

title: As Wardogs blows past 200k Steam concurrents, its developers are prepared for the day 'hype dies down'
summary: The way our hobby talks about player counts is all sorts of messed up. Steam concurrents are a useful metric for gauging a game's general popularity, but they paint an incomplete picture.
author: Morgan Park
keyHighlights: The way our hobby talks about player counts is all sorts of messed up.
"Wardogs will continue to lose players for months as the hype dies down," Brammer wrote .
In a video published last month outlining " 10 reasons not to buy Wardogs ," game director Howard Philpott expanded on Bulkhead's expectations:
fullContent: The way our hobby talks about player counts is all sorts of messed up. Steam concurrents are a useful metric for gauging a game's general popularity, but they paint an incomplete picture. They're a single data point, yet have become the flimsy scaffolding on which the internet builds elaborate headcanon about a game's quality, viability, or deadness. Sometimes dogpiling is so successful, and the resulting perception so difficult to fight, that simply saying a game is dead is enough to help kill it.

It's a trend that annoys me to no end, so it's refreshing to see a developer speaking openly about concurrents—both about how many it considers "healthy," and why it's normal for the number to rise and fall. It's been a recurring topic for Wardogs developer Bulkhead, whose closed beta surpassed 200,000 concurrents today on Steam. Responding to a TimTheTatman clip on X, CEO Joe Brammer spoke on the milsim's unexpected popularity, and its inevitable (but healthy) decline.

"Wardogs will continue to lose players for months as the hype dies down," Brammer wrote . "Doesn't make it a bad game or even a problem, we planned for 5k players concurrent! It'll maintain a healthy playerbase and we'll continue to build the 1.0 version of the game then... it'll boom again :) And so the cycle continues :)"

It's a cycle many of us are familiar with, but rarely acknowledge. I tend to build a rotation of multiplayer favorites that I regularly return to, either to check out an update or scratch an itch. It is, I think, a pretty healthy way to enjoy videogames, but the rise of live service "forever" games, as well as high-profile failures, have proliferated the idea that videogames are those species of shark that will die if they ever stop swimming.

Much like the majority of videogames before 2016, Bulkhead does not need Wardogs to be a consistent, top-charting megahit to continue making it. In a video published last month outlining " 10 reasons not to buy Wardogs ," game director Howard Philpott expanded on Bulkhead's expectations:

Ito is a horror icon and should be eternally proud of the work he's done for its unparalleled influence on the genre.
To be honest, lately, I’ve been thinking that if I hadn’t sacrificed my personal life, found a girlfriend, and gotten married early on, I probably would have been happier.
fullContent: "The 8 years I spent developing Silent Hill 1, 2 & 3 at Konami, I gave up on getting a girlfriend," reads a new tweet from Masahiro Ito, the legendary Team Silent artist best known for designing Silent Hill 2 antagonist Pyramid Head. The tweet largely echoes something Ito said back in 2024 about not having the time for a girlfriend when he was working at Konami, but now he straight-up suggests he regrets sacrificing his love life for the his work.
"Never even went on a single date w/ a lady," he says. "I sacrificed my days off & slept on cardboards spread out on the floor, but I never in my wildest dreams imagined I'd end up like this on X."

That is... incredibly sad. Ito is a horror icon and should be eternally proud of the work he's done for its unparalleled influence on the genre. That said, as a married man who wouldn't trade my family for the world, it's fair for him to long for love.
"To be honest, lately, I've been thinking that if I hadn't sacrificed my personal life, found a girlfriend, and gotten married early on, I probably would have been happier."

summary: If we end up seeing Deadpool in Marvel's Spider-Man 3, it would seem we have Peter Parker actor Yuri Lowenthal to thank, at least partly.
author: Jordan Gerblick
keyHighlights: If we end up seeing Deadpool in Marvel's Spider-Man 3, it would seem we have Peter Parker actor Yuri Lowenthal to thank, at least partly.

fullContent: If we end up seeing Deadpool in Marvel's Spider-Man 3, it would seem we have Peter Parker actor Yuri Lowenthal to thank, at least partly.

Talking to The Movie Dweeb on Instagram , Lowenthal was asked to comment on a potential Wolverine and Spider-Man collab in Insomniac's next open-world Spider-Man game. Insomniac is currently hard at work prepping for the release of Marvel's Wolverine , out September 15, but considering the success of Spider-Man, the standalone Miles Morales game, and Spider-Man 2, another Peter Parker game seems likely to happen at some point even though nothing's been confirmed yet. And of course, a Wolverine x Spider-Man match-up seems all the more likely with Insomniac now having worked on both IPs.
Lowenthal thinks a Wolverine collab would be "terribly exciting," but he says "there is one character that I would opt for even more strongly than Wolverine, and it would be Deadpool."

In response to this, The Movie Dweeb points out a tweet apparently published at some point from Insomniac creative director Brian Horton. I tried to track down the tweet, but Horton's Twitter account has been deactivated and there's no Bluesky equivalent, so take this with a grain of salt. According to The Movie Dweeb, the tweet read "worlds collide" and included hashtags for Wolverine and Spider-Man. Lowenthal says the tweet is news to him, but confirmed he's pushed Horton repeatedly on Deadpool being in the next Spider-Man game.

"I've pushed [Horton] every time I see him with the Deadpool thing, so if I've just spoiled it for Spider-Man 3, then I would just like to believe that they got the idea from me anyway," Lowenthal says.

title: Spider-Noir canceled after one season at Prime Video despite receiving 11 Emmy nominations
summary: Despite critical acclaim and a slew of Emmy nominations, Spider-Noir will not be returning for a second season at Prime Video.
author: Lauren Milici
keyHighlights: Despite critical acclaim and a slew of Emmy nominations, Spider-Noir will not be returning for a second season at Prime Video.
According to Deadline, there are still multiple projects on development, and one is "nearing a series order."
For more, check out our Spider-Noir review , or if you're still confused about how Spider-Noir is connected to the Spider-Verse movies , we've got the answer.
fullContent: Despite critical acclaim and a slew of Emmy nominations, Spider-Noir will not be returning for a second season at Prime Video.

Per Deadline , it seems like Amazon MGM Studios and Sony Pictures Television expected bigger streaming numbers when making their decision. But given recent reports that the first season's budget was somewhere around $400 million, I can see why the studios might've needed the show to become a megahit in order to justify spending that money on a second season.

Amazon and Sony are still moving ahead with their multi-title deal to use IP from Sony's Universe of Marvel characters. You might remember that the first Spider-Man spin-off, Silk: Spider-Society, was ultimately canceled before entering production. Spider-Noir is now the second canceled project... and there's a third on the way. According to Deadline, there are still multiple projects on development, and one is "nearing a series order." Details are, of course, being kept under wraps.

Spider-Noir saw Nicolas Cage as a jaded, down-on-his-luck private detective version of Ben Reilly aka the Spider, who finds himself returning to superheroism and going up against classic Rogue Gallery villains like Sandman and Silvermane. The series has a 91% on Rotten Tomatoes, with our own Spider-Noir review praising the show's originality and Cage's excellent and equally odd acting choices.

Spider-Noir is streaming now in both black-and-white and in color on Prime Video. For more, check out our Spider-Noir review , or if you're still confused about how Spider-Noir is connected to the Spider-Verse movies , we've got the answer.

title: "Top-down Zelda meets Bloodborne": action RPG Withering Realms is out now in early access, should you fancy riding the shoulders of a horrible doll
summary: Withering Rooms was an unexpectedly devious and absorbing slice of dollhouse action-RPG horror. As such, I've been looking forward to Withering Realms, the standalone sort-of-sequel, which launches in early access today.
author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
keyHighlights: Withering Rooms was an unexpectedly devious and absorbing slice of dollhouse action-RPG horror.
You play a ghost child, clinging to the shoulders of a living marionette.
You wouldn't accept if that thing offered you a piggyback.
fullContent: Withering Rooms was an unexpectedly devious and absorbing slice of dollhouse action-RPG horror. As such, I've been looking forward to Withering Realms, the standalone sort-of-sequel, which launches in early access today.

The new game takes place in the 1920s, following the 'premature' end of World War 1 thanks to an occult catastrophe. You play a ghost child, clinging to the shoulders of a living marionette. The marionette is a real fright, its body a coatful of springs and hinges, its face a one-eyed rictus: it reminds me of certain scenes from Phil Tippett's stop motion masterpiece Mad God and also, of Curly from Mouthwashing . You wouldn't accept if that thing offered you a piggyback. But it is pretty handy in a fight.
